subject.title: Backup: add encrypted snapshot backup flow

question: Should OpenClaw core accept a native folder-backed encrypted snapshot backup flow after the security/proof blockers are fixed, or should this remain local archive support plus ClawHub/plugin backup integrations?
rationale: The PR adds new core backup config, secret handling, command aliases, and destructive restore behavior; that is larger than a routine bug fix and needs owner direction once correctness blockers are resolved.

options.title: Sponsor native flow after hardening
options.body: Keep this direction open, require rebase, security fixes, upgrade proof, and real setup/run/list/restore evidence before merge.

options.title: Narrow to archive hardening only
options.body: Reject the new snapshot/config surface for now and ask for smaller PRs that improve the existing local export/verify path.

options.title: Move richer backup to ClawHub
options.body: Leave OpenClaw core on local archives and direct encrypted/off-machine snapshot workflows to a plugin, skill, or service integration.

recommendation.title: Sponsor native flow after hardening
recommendation.body: Keep this direction open, require rebase, security fixes, upgrade proof, and real setup/run/list/restore evidence before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent backup hardening history on current main and are a practical routing point for the core backup boundary decision.
